deck_name: 君の名は。 Ch.4 探訪 — Grammar & Expressions
source: 新海誠『君の名は。』(角川つばさ文庫), 第4章「探訪」
notes: 瀧 travels to Hida with 司 and 奥寺先輩 to find 三葉's town from his sketches, learns that 糸守町 was destroyed by a comet fragment three years earlier, and reads the archives and the list of the dead as his memories start to fade. This deck covers the patterns that carry those scenes: searching (〜を頼りに, 〜て回る, 〜たところ), the formal register of news and reference books (〜により, 〜とされる, 〜に及ぶ), disbelief (〜とは, 〜はずがない, 〜はずなのに), reasoning out the time gap (〜ことになる) and memory slipping away (〜につれて, 〜一方だ, 〜さえ, 〜っけ). The list is built from the chapter's scenes and the novel's style, not transcribed page by page, so a few items may sit a chapter early or late.

priority_guide.high: Learn before or while reading this chapter — it carries the scene.
priority_guide.medium: Useful; context usually helps if you forget it.
priority_guide.low: Recognition is enough — look it up once, don't over-drill.

difficulty_guide.two_above: N1 / literary — ambitious; learn to recognise it.

kanji_difficulty_guide.easy: Kanji are common; readable at N3.
kanji_difficulty_guide.medium: One or more kanji may trip you — drill the reading.
kanji_difficulty_guide.hard: Rare kanji or irregular reading — learn the kana form first.

cards.pattern: (Nと / Nに) 連絡がつく / つかない
cards.scene: The chapter starts from the fact that 瀧 can no longer reach 三葉 by any means.
cards.context: Form: (Nと / Nに) 連絡がつく — intransitive つく means 'to get through, to be established'. 連絡がつかない stresses the failed result (calls not connecting, no reply), whereas 連絡しない just means not making contact. Similar: 電話がつながらない.
cards.example_sentence: 三葉に何度電話しても、まったく連絡がつかない。
cards.example_reading: みつは に なんど でんわ して も、 まったく れんらく が つかない。
cards.example_meaning: However many times he calls 三葉, he can't get through to her at all.

cards.pattern: N + を頼りに(して) + V
cards.scene: 瀧 sets off to find the town with nothing but his memory and his sketches to guide him.
cards.context: Form: N + を頼りに(して) + action. You depend on something thin or fragile to find your way: 地図を頼りに, 記憶を頼りに, 月明かりを頼りに. Compare 〜をもとに (based on, using as material) — 〜を頼りに stresses dependence and uncertainty.
cards.example_sentence: 瀧は記憶だけを頼りに、何枚も風景の絵を描いた。
cards.example_reading: たき は きおく だけ を たより に、 なんまい も ふうけい の え を かいた。
cards.example_meaning: Relying on nothing but memory, 瀧 drew picture after picture of the scenery.

meanings: ~ from place to place / person to person
cards.pattern: Vて + 回る
cards.scene: The three go around showing the sketches and asking everyone they meet.
cards.context: Form: Vて-form + 回る. Adds 'all over, one place or person after another': 聞いて回る, 探して回る, 謝って回る. The compound 〜歩く (探し歩く, 聞き歩く) is similar but emphasises going on foot.
cards.example_sentence: 三人は絵を持って、町じゅうの店を聞いて回った。
cards.example_reading: さんにん は え を もって、 まちじゅう の みせ を きいて まわった。
cards.example_meaning: The three took the drawing and went around asking at every shop in town.

cards.pattern: Vます-stem + 果てる
cards.scene: The three end a fruitless day worn out, and later find a town changed beyond recognition.
cards.context: Form: Vます-stem + 果てる (果てる = to come to an end). Pushes a negative state to its limit: 疲れ果てる (worn out), 困り果てる (at one's wits' end), 変わり果てる (changed beyond recognition), 荒れ果てる (fall into ruin). Literary; compare the neutral 〜きる (使いきる = use up).
cards.example_sentence: 長い間だれも住まず、家はすっかり荒れ果てていた。
cards.example_reading: ながい あいだ だれ も すまず、 いえ は すっかり あれはてて いた。
cards.example_meaning: No one had lived there for years, and the house had fallen into complete ruin.

meanings: when I did ~, (it turned out that)
cards.pattern: Vた + ところ、(discovered result)
cards.scene: When they show the sketch to the ramen shop owner, the result is finally different — he knows the place.
cards.context: Form: Vた-form + ところ, followed by a result that was discovered. Narrative, slightly formal: 'I did X, and found that Y.' Unlike 〜たら, the second half must be a fact that actually happened, never a request or intention. Don't confuse it with 〜たところだ (have just done).
cards.example_sentence: 店主に絵を見せたところ、すぐに町の名前がわかった。
cards.example_reading: てんしゅ に え を みせた ところ、 すぐ に まち の なまえ が わかった。
cards.example_meaning: When we showed the owner the drawing, we learned the town's name right away.

cards.pattern: N + により、clause / N + による + N
cards.scene: Accounts of the disaster — from the owner and in print — describe the town destroyed by the falling fragment.
cards.context: Form: N + により (linking two clauses) or N + による + noun (彗星による被害). The formal, written counterpart of 〜で for cause or means, standard in news. It also marks the agent of a passive in formal writing: 隕石によりできた湖.
cards.example_sentence: 彗星の破片の落下により、町の大部分が失われた。
cards.example_reading: すいせい の はへん の らっか に より、 まち の だいぶぶん が うしなわれた。
cards.example_meaning: Due to the fall of the comet fragment, most of the town was lost.

cards.pattern: N (number / range) + に及ぶ
cards.scene: The death toll described by the owner and the archives runs into the hundreds.
cards.context: Form: N + に及ぶ / に及んだ; before a noun: 数百人に及ぶ犠牲者. Stresses that a figure or range is strikingly large: 被害は町全体に及んだ. Related: 〜に及ばない (not equal to / no need to). Similar news verb: 〜に上る (amount to).
cards.example_sentence: 大雨の被害は、県内の広い地域に及んだ。
cards.example_reading: おおあめ の ひがい は、 けんない の ひろい ちいき に およんだ。
cards.example_meaning: The damage from the heavy rain extended across a wide area of the prefecture.

cards.pattern: 言葉を失う (≈ 言葉が出ない)
cards.scene: Looking over the ruined town, 瀧 and his friends are lost for words.
cards.context: Form: fixed phrase 言葉を失う (literary), ≈ 言葉が出ない or the formal 絶句する. Used for shock or horror, and also for overwhelming beauty. Here 失う takes an abstract object.
cards.example_sentence: あまりに美しい景色に、私たちは言葉を失った。
cards.example_reading: あまり に うつくしい けしき に、 わたしたち は ことば を うしなった。
cards.example_meaning: We were left speechless by the breathtaking view.

cards.pattern: plain form / N + とは(…)
cards.scene: 瀧 can hardly take in that the lively town he remembers was destroyed three years ago.
cards.context: Form: plain form (or N) + とは, often trailing off or followed by 思わなかった / 驚いた. Expresses shock that something is actually the case. Stronger and more written than 〜なんて; don't confuse it with defining 〜とは (愛とは何か = what is love?).
cards.example_sentence: まさか、あの町がもう存在しないとは。
cards.example_reading: まさか、 あの まち が もう そんざい しない とは。
cards.example_meaning: To think that town no longer exists…

cards.pattern: plain form + はずがない (Nの / なA-な + はずがない)
cards.scene: 瀧 refuses to accept what he is told: 三葉 cannot have died three years ago when he was with her so recently.
cards.context: Form: V / いA plain form + はずがない; Nの / なA-な + はずがない. The speaker's logical certainty that something cannot be true. 〜わけがない is close but more emotional and colloquial; そんなはずはない is the stock reaction of disbelief.
cards.example_sentence: そんなことが本当に起きたはずがない、と彼は首を振った。
cards.example_reading: そんな こと が ほんとう に おきた はず が ない、 と かれ は くび を ふった。
cards.example_meaning: 'That can't really have happened,' he said, shaking his head.

meanings: ~ ought to be the case, and yet
cards.pattern: plain form + はずなのに (Nの / なA-な + はずなのに)
cards.scene: 瀧 was talking with 三葉 only recently — so she should be alive, and yet the town and the records say otherwise.
cards.context: Form: plain form + はず + なのに. Combines expectation (はず) with frustrated contrast (のに): the facts contradict what you are sure is true. Past variant 〜はずだったのに = it was supposed to …, but.
cards.example_sentence: ついこの前まで話していたはずなのに、名前が思い出せない。
cards.example_reading: つい この まえ まで はなして いた はず なのに、 なまえ が おもいだせない。
cards.example_meaning: We were talking just the other day, and yet I can't remember her name.

meanings: as one keeps ~ing, before one knows it
cards.pattern: Vている + うちに、(unplanned change)
cards.scene: As 瀧 stares at his phone, the diary entries change and disappear before his eyes.
cards.context: Form: Vている + うちに + a change nobody planned (〜てくる / 〜ていく / 〜なる). Different from 若いうちに (do it while you still can): here the change creeps in during an ongoing action. Compare the neutral time span 〜間に.
cards.example_sentence: 画面を見ているうちに、文字が一つずつ消えていった。
cards.example_reading: がめん を みて いる うち に、 もじ が ひとつ ずつ きえて いった。
cards.example_meaning: As I watched the screen, the characters disappeared one by one.

cards.pattern: plain form / N + とされる・とされている
cards.scene: The library's books and articles state facts in a formal register — the lake's origin, the comet's period, the official toll.
cards.context: Form: plain form (だ is usually dropped after N / なA) + とされる / とされている. The passive of とする: an accepted or official view, typical of news, textbooks and reference books. More authoritative than 〜と言われている.
cards.example_sentence: この湖は、大昔に落ちた隕石によってできたとされている。
cards.example_reading: この みずうみ は、 おおむかし に おちた いんせき に よって できた と されて いる。
cards.example_meaning: This lake is believed to have been formed by a meteorite that fell long ago.

cards.pattern: plain form + ことになる
cards.scene: Working back from the dates, 瀧 sees what they imply: the 三葉 he knew was living three years in the past.
cards.context: Form: plain form + ことになる. Besides 'it has been decided that' (the N3 use), it states a logical conclusion: if A, that amounts to B. Often with つまり or 〜とすると, and as 〜ということになる.
cards.example_sentence: あの日が三年前だとすると、二人は違う時間を生きていたことになる。
cards.example_reading: あの ひ が さんねん まえ だ と する と、 ふたり は ちがう じかん を いきて いた こと に なる。
cards.example_meaning: If that day was three years ago, it means the two of them were living in different times.

cards.pattern: V dictionary form / N + につれて
cards.scene: The more time passes after the shock, the more 瀧's memories of 三葉 slip away.
cards.context: Form: V dictionary form / noun of change (時間, 成長) + につれて (written: につれ). Both halves must be gradual changes: 時間がたつにつれて記憶が薄れる. 〜にしたがって is a slightly more formal near-synonym; 〜とともに also works.
cards.example_sentence: 夜が更けるにつれて、彼女の顔がぼやけていった。
cards.example_reading: よ が ふける に つれて、 かのじょ の かお が ぼやけて いった。
cards.example_meaning: As the night wore on, her face grew blurrier in his mind.

cards.pattern: V dictionary form + 一方だ
cards.scene: No matter how hard 瀧 tries, his memory of 三葉 only keeps fading.
cards.context: Form: V dictionary form (change verbs: 増える, 減る, 悪くなる, 薄れる) + 一方だ. A trend moving in one direction only, usually an unwelcome one. Compare 〜ばかりだ (similar, a little more emotional) and 一方で (on the other hand).
cards.example_sentence: 思い出そうとすればするほど、記憶は薄れる一方だった。
cards.example_reading: おもいだそう と すれば する ほど、 きおく は うすれる いっぽう だった。
cards.example_meaning: The harder he tried to remember, the more the memory just kept fading.

cards.pattern: plain past / だった + っけ; 〜んだっけ
cards.scene: At the inn, 瀧 struggles to recall the name of the girl he came all this way to find.
cards.context: Form: plain past (〜た / だった) + っけ, or 〜んだっけ. Used when trying to recall something you once knew, or checking it with someone. Casual; the polite version is 〜でしたっけ. Soft and self-directed — the sound of a memory slipping.
cards.example_sentence: あの子の名前、何だったっけ。
cards.example_reading: あの こ の なまえ、 なん だった っけ。
cards.example_meaning: What was that girl's name again?

cards.pattern: N (+ particle) + さえ (+ negative)
cards.scene: 瀧 realises he can't even remember the name of the girl he has been searching for.
cards.context: Form: N (+ particle, e.g. にさえ) + さえ, very often with a negative: 名前さえ思い出せない. Picks out an extreme case — if not even this, then nothing else either. 〜すら is more literary; 〜も is neutral. Keep it apart from conditional 〜さえ〜ば (if only).
cards.example_sentence: あんなに何度も呼んだ名前さえ、もう思い出せない。
cards.example_reading: あんな に なんど も よんだ なまえ さえ、 もう おもいだせない。
cards.example_meaning: I can no longer remember even the name I called so many times.

cards.pattern: Vます-stem + かける / Vます-stem + かけの + N
cards.scene: Her name almost comes back to 瀧 — he begins to say it, and it is gone.
cards.context: Form: Vます-stem + かける (verb) or かけの + N (食べかけのパン = a half-eaten roll). An action begun but not finished, or on the verge of happening: 言いかける, 忘れかける, 死にかける. Related 〜かかる: 喉まで出かかる (be about to come out).
cards.example_sentence: 何か言いかけて、彼はそのまま黙ってしまった。
cards.example_reading: なにか いいかけて、 かれ は そのまま だまって しまった。
cards.example_meaning: He started to say something, then fell silent.

cards.pattern: Vない-stem + ぬ (する → せぬ)
cards.scene: Fits the narration's literary touches, such as describing 瀧's sleepless night at the inn.
cards.context: Form: ない-stem + ぬ (行かぬ, 知らぬ, 眠れぬ; する → せぬ). A classical negative that survives in writing and set phrases: 思わぬ出来事, 眠れぬ夜, 見知らぬ人. Same meaning as 〜ない, but before a noun it gives a literary, dramatic tone. Related: 〜ず / 〜ずに.
cards.example_sentence: 思わぬところで、昔の友人に再会した。
cards.example_reading: おもわぬ ところ で、 むかし の ゆうじん に さいかい した。
cards.example_meaning: I ran into an old friend in an unexpected place.
